message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower from scratch would be a massive undertaking—think of a 300‑meter‑tall lattice structure with thousands of steel panels, rivets, and exposed surfaces. Even though the tower is routinely repainted every 7–10 years (to protect against rust), a full repaint from the ground up would involve:

| Task | Rough Time |
|------|------------|
| **Preparation** (cleaning, rust removal, surface prep) | 2–3 weeks |
| **Primer application** (multiple coats, drying time) | 1–2 weeks |
| **Topcoat layers** (two or more coats, each drying 24–48 h) | 1–2 weeks |
| **Detail work** (painting railings, decorative elements, signage) | 1–2 weeks |
| **Inspection & touch‑ups** | 1 week |

Adding safety measures (fall protection, scaffolding, cranes), logistics (transporting paint, equipment), and weather delays, a realistic estimate for a complete overhaul would be **around 8–12 weeks** (roughly 2–3 months).  

If you’re asking about a one‑off “spray‑paint” style job (e.g., a temporary art installation), the time could be shorter—perhaps a few days—but it would still require permits, safety plans, and coordination with the Paris authorities.
